newsitem.title: RWANDA: Rwanda rejects reports of troops in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Rwanda rejects reports of troops in Zaire.

text.p: Rwanda rejected Belgium raising on Wednesday reports of the presence of Rwandan troops in Zaire, saying Kigali had no troops there and did not intend to send in any.
"The Belgian announcement is very unfortunate because it is baseless," said Claude Dusaidi, political advisor to Vice -President and Defence Minister Major-General Paul Kagame.
"We cannot understand why Belgium is accusing Rwanda of intervening in Zaire. Our position is clear. We have no troops in Zaire, we never had any and we don't intend to have any."
In Brussels, the foreign ministry said it was concerned at reports about the presence of foreign troops including Rwandans in Zaire which, if confirmed, would be totally unacceptable.

"We are receiving more and more reports about the presence of regular Rwandan troops in eastern Zaire. If these can be confirmed, this would be an unacceptable violation of the territorial integrity of Zaire," spokesman Andre Querton said.
He said the reports spoke of a "meaningful number" of Rwandan units in the Kivu area, who had moved into the region after the seizure of eastern Zaire by Zairean rebels.

Zaire has repeatedly accused Uganda, Rwanda and Burundi of backing rebels of the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (ADFL), led by veteran opposition politician Laurent Kabila.

Commenting on a statement by the military high command in Kinshasa alleging that several thousand Ugandan troops had invaded Zaire, Querton said this too would be a violation of the country's territorial integrity.
Uganda said the Zairean allegations were false.
"I think that what is worrying the Belgians is that the Zairean and ex-FAR (former Rwandan Hutu) troops are having a hard time against the rebels," Dusaidi told Reuters in Kigali.
"When Belgium sees the Zairean counter-offensive crumble they have to attribute the rebel success to other countries."
"We have made it clear since last year that we don't want to be dragged into Zairean problems," he added.
Rwandan troops entered eastern Zaire at least twice in the early stages of the rebellion since in October, witnesses said. But Kigali rejected reports of a long-term Rwandan presence.
